speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodic cough and shortness of breath; to help me narrow down your condition, can you describe exactly what triggers these episodes and how long they last?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age and the recent viral symptoms, could you tell me if you have ever been diagnosed with asthma or if you have any known allergies? REQUEST TEST: Pulmonary_Function_Tests.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The spirometry confirms an obstructive pattern, and the worsening at night suggests nocturnal symptoms common in asthma, but the recent viral illness raises concern for post-infectious airway hyperreactivity or bronchiolitis obliterans.
